items.stem: A renewal epoch Sₙ is:
options: The cumulative time of the nth renewal
items.explanation: Sₙ is the sum of the first n inter-renewal times.

items.stem: The ordinary renewal model assumes cycle lengths are:
items.explanation: The ordinary model uses iid positive cycle lengths.

items.stem: N(t) counts:
items.explanation: N(t) counts epochs Sₙ not exceeding t.

items.stem: The renewal function m(t) is:
items.explanation: The renewal function is the expected renewal count.

items.stem: If every gap is exactly 3 units, find N(10).
items.explanation: Renewals occur at 3, 6 and 9; N(10)=3.

items.stem: If the mean gap is 4 hours, the long-run rate per hour is:
items.explanation: The long-run rate is 1/μ=1/4.

items.stem: N(t)≥n is equivalent to:
items.explanation: At least n renewals have occurred if the nth epoch is at most t.

items.stem: IID exponential gaps with rate λ produce:
items.explanation: Exponential iid inter-arrival times characterise a Poisson process.

items.stem: The elementary renewal theorem states:
items.explanation: It is an asymptotic expected renewal rate result.

items.stem: The renewal-reward rate is:
items.explanation: Expected reward per cycle divided by expected cycle duration.

items.stem: Which statements are correct? A. Epochs are cumulative sums. B. N(t) is random for random gaps. C. m(t)=E[N(t)]. D. Mean gap is the long-run rate.
items.explanation: A, B and C are true; long-run rate is reciprocal mean gap.
statements: Renewal counts are random for random gaps.
The renewal function is expected renewal count.
Mean gap itself is the long-run rate.

A.why: Sₙ is the cumulative sum of gaps.

B.why: The count depends on random epochs.

D.why: The rate is reciprocal mean gap.

items.stem: If X is 1 with probability 1/4 and 3 with probability 3/4, find E[X].
For the previous gap distribution, find the long-run rate.
items.explanation: The rate is 1/2.5=0.4.

items.stem: For a Poisson process viewed as a renewal process, which are true? A. Gaps are iid. B. Gaps are exponential. C. E[N(t)]=λt. D. Every renewal process is Poisson.
items.explanation: A, B and C are true; general renewal processes need not be Poisson.
statements: Renewal counts are random for random gaps.
The renewal function is expected renewal count.
Mean gap itself is the long-run rate.

A.why: Sₙ is the cumulative sum of gaps.

B.why: The count depends on random epochs.

D.why: The rate is reciprocal mean gap.

items.stem: Expected reward is 60 and expected cycle duration is 4 hours. Find the reward rate.
items.explanation: 60/4=15 units per hour.

items.stem: If N(t)=n, which relation holds?
items.explanation: Exactly n renewals means the nth epoch occurred but the next did not.

items.stem: If every gap is 2.5 units, find N(9).
items.explanation: Epochs at 2.5, 5 and 7.5 occurred; the fourth is at 10.

items.stem: Two renewal models have the same finite mean gap. Which is generally true?
options: Their long-run rates agree but finite-time counts may differ
items.explanation: The long-run rate depends on the mean; finite-time counts depend on the full distribution.

items.stem: Which statements about renewal-reward are correct? A. It uses expected reward per cycle. B. It divides by expected cycle length. C. It gives a long-run rate. D. It is E[X]/E[R].
items.explanation: A, B and C are true; the ratio is E[R]/E[X].

The renewal function is expected renewal count.
Mean gap itself is the long-run rate.

A.why: Sₙ is the cumulative sum of gaps.

B.why: The count depends on random epochs.

D.why: The rate is reciprocal mean gap.

items.stem: Mean gap is 8 minutes. Find the long-run renewal rate per hour.
items.explanation: 60/8=7.5 renewals per hour.
